results.method: Aggregation of the six W8 final-test measurements (EV-20261116-dataset-raid, -mage, -beemo, -detectrl-x, -ghostwriter, -opai-bench). Every per-slice value is quoted verbatim from its source run artifact (Wilson 95% uppers as recorded there) and independently re-verified: the Wilson 95% interval is recomputed with textforensics.probe_metrics.wilson_ci from the recorded (k, n) and must agree within 5e-4 (the source artifacts round Wilson uppers to 4 decimals in the A/C artifacts and to 6 decimals in the B artifacts). The detector was NOT re-run for this artifact; independent re-scoring is established by the reproduction artifacts (worker E AGREE on all five A/C corpora; worker B AGREE on DetectRL-X). Human FPR = P(verdict=ai_like | human); native TPR = P(verdict=ai_like | AI) at the same native operating point (builtin-heuristic native verdict via analyze_text; no score threshold). Intervals are Wilson 95% CIs (z=1.96). Slices with n_human = 0 are listed separately under unmeasured_slices with a null FPR and a stated reason; they are not measured slices. The pooled_documents_only value pools only the six disjoint pooled per-dataset slices (0/4194); finer slices overlap the pooled slices by construction and are never pooled.

notes:
Pooling is NOT legitimate as the gate statistic. The slices differ in regime (raw vs human-edited), language (en vs mul 8-language vs en+de), domain, generator vintage and editing; pooling hides that heterogeneity. The pooled 0/4194 number is reported for completeness only. The release gate must use the per-slice worst Wilson ci_upper among the document slices — a single pooled number would let a large slice (DetectRL-X, n=2400) mask a thin slice (MAGE testbed:dialogsum, n=3, Wilson upper 0.5615).

Worst document slice: MAGE testbed:dialogsum, 0/3 human rows verdict ai_like, Wilson 95% upper 0.5615. It is tied with MAGE testbed:pubmed (0/3, upper 0.5615); the alphabetically-first slice wins the tie-break, per worker C's precedent (GhostWriter arxiv_papers vs euro_court_cases, both 0/26, upper 0.1287). The worst slice is worst by small-n Wilson bound, not by observed false positives: every slice in this aggregation has k_fp = 0.

Still unknown:
- Worst-slice human FPR as a *supported* claim: the worst document slice (MAGE testbed:dialogsum, n_human=3, Wilson upper 0.5615) fails the FPR bar outright (n_human below the 100-row minimum; Wilson upper above the 0.05 ceiling). The report-card lead ('worst-slice human FPR = unknown') changes only by a parent decision; this artifact does not change it.
- Human FPR on slices the W8 final-test sets do not cover at all: the 43 unmeasured slices listed in unmeasured_slices (n_human = 0 in final-test), non-English document text outside DetectRL-X/GhostWriter, ESL human text, texts below 80 words, generators newer than each record's declared vintage, and human populations outside the declared ones.
- Whether the zero observed false positives persist on larger human samples: every Wilson upper bound here is a bound on zero events, not a measured positive rate.

This artifact aggregates the W8 final-test measurements; it is not a new claim and it does not change the report-card lead: the gate reads results["worst_slice_human_fpr"] for the lead, and this artifact deliberately carries no such key — 0.5615 is the Wilson 95% upper bound on a 0/3 rate (MAGE testbed:dialogsum), not a measured FPR point rate. No claim cites this record; the worst-slice human FPR as a supported claim remains unknown.
